text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish construction company Peab has stopped work on a tunnel in Norway to Oslo's new airport because of a conflict about how much the project will cost.
- There is no better base between the United States and Latin America than Miami, Florida, say Swedish businessmen who run businesses from the fast-growing region.

- Sweden, which gives 0.77 percent of its Gross Domestic Product to developing countries, now ranks fourth among most generous donor nations after Denmark, Norway and The Netherlands, World Bank statistics show. Private investors are investing more money in these countries than before, however.

- The Swedish government will present a program on Tuesday to support the town of Arboga after Volvo Aero, the aircraft engine division of automotive group Volvo, which moved its Arboga operations to its plant in Trollhattan. The program could include moving parts of the defence equipment authority to Arboga from Stockholm in an effort to help create jobs in the region.

- Norway is ready to build gas plants to replace the power Sweden will lose when closing down the Barseback nuclear power plant. The two Norwegian oil and gas companies Statoil and Saga Petroleum are interested in cooperating with Swedish power companies Sydkraft, Goteborg Energi and Vattenfall to build one or more gas plants on Sweden's western coast. The government and two other parties have agreed to close down one of Barseback's two reactors in 1998 and the other at a later stage.

- Shares in Swedish information technology companies have slumped by up to 38 percent since their 1997 peak because of exaggerated expectations about the companies' profits and weak performance by U.S. IT shares.
- A reshuffle in the board of Swedish state-owned utility Vattenfall is expected at the company's annual meeting in May.
- The average age for boards of listed Swedish companies is increasing. In 26 companies it is more than 60 years.
